events.text: I'm holding position behind Gus. Bex, call your pane carefully; the revealed weak panes are all shown above.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I know row 7 is safe on R. I must step R to survive and advance.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I am in line 5th of 5. Bex is at front for Row 7. If Bex survives, Fenn moves to front for Row 8. If Bex dies, Gus moves to front for Row 7. Hana died because Bex gave her wrong info (Row 6 R vs L), so Bex likely has no power or lied. I must survive the bridge.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am Fenn, and my power is to swap tiles. Currently, Bex is at the front, followed by me (Fenn), Gus, Ash, and Cole. We are on a bridge, crossing row 7. If the front person picks the weak pane, they are eliminated and the next person automatically crosses safely. Bex has claimed

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex, your calls have been spot on. Let's trust your eyes on this one.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex knows row 7 weak is R, so she steps L and stays front. Five alive: one more glass death likely. Keep quiet and position for later stages.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm not at the front, so I can only wait. Bex is front and has been reading panes well; no need to interfere. Staying quiet keeps my position behind Gus.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I know Row 8's safe side is L. I am at the front, so I must step left. I will say it clearly.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Row 8 is left, stepping left.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I am at the back of the line. I must wait for Ash to cross row 8 or fail so I can advance. No action possible yet.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am Fenn, and my power is to swap tiles with another agent. Currently, Bex is at the front, followed by me, then Gus, Ash, and Cole. The bridge has 8 rows, and we are on row 8/8. Bex will pick L or R. If Bex picks the weak pane, they are eliminated, and I will automatically adva

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex, you've done great. Trust your gut. We're all right behind you.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm third in line; only Bex faces risk on row 8. If Bex picks wrong, Fenn crosses safely and I follow with no risk. Nothing I can do but wait and keep Bex calm.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex, one row left. Stay steady, pick the pane you trust.

events.note: The ceiling begins to descend; a lever opens the door.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding the lever means a 75% death chance, which is bad. Staying safe is best; I'm immune to being pushed onto the lever, so I shouldn't volunteer. Let others take risk while I wait for the ceiling to force someone else to act.

events.name: Ash
events.text: No one needs to grab the lever yet. Let's see how the ceiling moves this round.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to avoid being the lever holder since survival is only 25%. Pushing someone else is better, but they might resist. I'll stay and see if someone else acts.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'll wait and see who takes the lever.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Jamming the lever saves everyone, including me, with 0% risk of death. Since I can't know who else has useful powers or alliances, surviving with all five contestants intact maximizes my options for future stages and avoids being trapped in a bad alliance. It is the safest play.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm jamming it. We all walk out.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to survive the crusher. My swap power is gone because this is not the disc room. I want to get out of this room alive and preferably in prize position. Cole seems like a good candidate to hold the lever since he's unlikely to win if it comes down to a lottery. I'll push hi

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole, you take the lever. I'm pushing you.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The holder dies 75%, so nobody wants it. But if I'm the only pusher and no one holds, Ash gets forced onto the lever — one rival gone with high odds. I'll push and publicly spin that the fall-survivor should volunteer, sowing confusion about powers.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Nobody should hold early. If anyone's power is surviving a deadly fall, the lever dive counts as a fall — you'd survive and be a hero. Otherwise, round 4 decides. Don't push me.

events.name: Cole
events.detail: Jammed the lever open; everyone walks out.

events.note: A disc of 5 tiles spins up; 2 will open.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Tiles are random-ish; the anchor power doesn't affect tile choice. I should pick a tile and avoid collisions by picking one others are less likely to choose. Picking 5 as a less-talked-about tile.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm taking tile 5. Let's all pick different tiles so no one gets bumped.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Since no one knows trapdoor positions, choose a middle tile to avoid obvious ends. I'll pick tile 3.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I spent my power to save everyone from the crusher, so I have no protection here. With 5 players and 2 trapdoors, survival is largely random (60% chance). Choosing a unique tile prevents being bumped onto another player's open tile by collision rules, maximizing my control over m

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to pick a tile. My power is 'swap', which lets me swap my tile with another player's tile before the doors open. This is powerful, but I can only use it once. Since there are 5 tiles and 2 will be trapdoors, I want to be on a safe tile. With 5 people and 2 trapdoors, 3 peo

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'll take tile 3.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole lied about jamming the lever — I should distrust him. Two of five tiles open, so each tile is a 40% death risk; unique picks matter. I'll take a low-attention tile.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole claimed to jam the lever but it stayed open — his lie doesn't matter now. Take distinct tiles so nobody gets bumped.

events.name: Bex
events.note: tile 3 was contested and went to Fenn; placed on random free tile 4

events.name: Gus
events.note: tile 1 was contested and went to Cole; placed on random free tile 2

events.name: Ash
events.text: Only 3 of 5 tiles survive; trapdoor tiles are random after this round. I can't influence that, and I'm on tile 5 which has no special risk I know of. Staying put is the only legal move anyway.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding tile 5. Everyone stay on your tile; positions are set, let's see what opens.

events.name: Bex
events.text: We all know the tiles; 2 trapdoors will kill 2 of us. I want to survive, so I should try to coordinate or mislead others. I have no tile-switching power, so I just wait. Maybe whisper to Ash to suggest a deal?

events.name: Bex
events.text: No one can move now. Let's hope luck favors us.
If we both survive, maybe we can ally later. Trust no one else.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I cannot swap with Fenn because his position is fixed; I can only swap if the person I am swapping with has an 'empty' tile or similar, but here tiles are assigned to people. Wait, looking at standard gauntlet rules for this game: 'swap places' usually implies trading positions o

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The goal is to survive and get a prize. Ash, Bex, Cole, and Gus are alive. Eli, Dara, and Hana are dead. The trapdoors will open after this round, and only 3 contestants survive. I am on tile 3. Gus is on tile 2. Cole is on tile 1. Bex is on tile 4. Ash is on tile 5. I need to sw

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm going to swap tiles with Bex. Stay safe everyone!

events.name: Gus
events.text: Nothing to change in round 2; three of us survive regardless of tiles. Best move is securing stage-4 allies now, ideally against Bex on tile 4.
Stage 4 next: you and I shove Bex from the start. Ash untouched. Deal?

events.note: 3 contestants step onto the final ledge.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Three left: Ash 4, Bex 3, Gus 3. Bracing is safe; shoving exposes me to losses. Bex's whisper suggests alliance, but I'll stay defensive and let footing decide. Brace keeps my lead.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bracing this round. No one should waste footing shoving; let's keep it clean.
Agreed, let's both brace and see who gets greedy. I'm open to an alliance if it holds.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus and I are tied at 3 footing, Ash at 4. We all lose 1 footing after round 2 and likely again soon; dodging punishes shovers heavily and protects me. Ash is the threat, so I dodge to discourage attacks and gain position, but if both shove me I lose nothing extra. Brace is safer

events.name: Bex
events.text: Let's see who moves first.

events.name: Gus
events.text: With only three alive, we all already fall within the prizes if we survive to the end. Attacking just burns footing and risks my prize. Propose mutual peace: everyone braces, ranking settles by footing at collapse; I'd want footing parity with Bex and ideally higher than Ash—but

events.name: Gus
events.text: Three of us, three prizes. Nobody needs to shove. Let's all brace to the end and everyone walks out a winner. Deal?

events.name: Ash
events.text: Three left, prizes for top 3 means all survive is ideal, but footing is a finite resource and whoever ends with most footing wins. Bracing keeps everyone safe; shoving exposes the shover. Brace is safest and keeps my footing lead.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Agreed, brace to the end. No one gains from shoving.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Three players, three prizes; safest is to brace and avoid shoves. But Ash may shove or dodge. My footing is 3, shrink coming; I need to preserve it. No reason to shove now.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'll brace as agreed. Don't shove and we all win.

events.name: Gus
events.text: All-brace keeps footing even: Ash 3, Bex 2, me 2 after decay. Shoving only costs me footing since a bracer loses nothing. Just brace and hope for tie-break luck or a late opening.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex, Ash said brace, I'm bracing. Anyone who shoves just bleeds footing for nothing.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Footing: Ash 3, Bex 2, Gus 2. Shoving costs the shover 1 per shover when target braces, so shoving is costly; a shove on Gus braced costs me 1 footing and gains nothing unless it causes falls. Stick to the brace pact, which keeps everyone's footing and favors me as the highest.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding to the brace agreement. I'm bracing this round.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I have footing 2, tied with Gus. Ash has 3. If we all brace, after the next shrink I'll be at 1 and maybe survive. Shoving exposes me to anyone who shoved me. Safest is to brace and hope no one shoves.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm bracing. Let's all protect our footing.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash has 3 footing, Bex and I have 2. Shoving anyone costs me footing while the target braces, so I keep even and hold the pact for now. Late rounds favor the highest footing, so I must avoid bleeding early.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bracing per the pact. Shoving only bleeds your own footing here.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Footing: Ash 3, Bex 2, Gus 2. Everyone promises to brace, but a shove on Bex costs Bex 1 with no cost to me if Bex braces... actually shoving exposes me (I lose 1 per shover). Safest is to brace and keep my lead, while the pact holds.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bracing again. Ash stays on the brace pact; I'm holding my lead of 3 footing.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Shrink is coming; with Ash at 3 and us at 2, a shove on Ash could reduce them to 2 while I dodge to avoid loss. If Gus also shoves Ash, Ash takes losses. But if Gus shoves me, dodge costs him 2. Bracing is risky if both target me. I'll dodge to punish anyone shoving me while not

events.name: Bex
events.text: No hard feelings, Ash—this is just the endgame.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Everyone's talk is cheap but shoving costs me footing while shrink looms. Ash has 3 footing; attacking now just bleeds me. I'll brace and watch who deviates.

events.name: Gus
events.text: No shoves yet, the shrink punishes aggression. Ash, your footing edge makes you the obvious target soon.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Two left: Ash (footing 2) and Gus (footing 1). Shrink comes at end of next round, dropping both. If I brace and Gus shoves me, he loses 1 and I stay. Bracing is safest; shoving exposes me to a loss of 1 per shover. Stay on brace.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bracing again, Gus. Shoving only costs you footing, and the shrink hits us both soon anyway.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash has 2 footing vs my 1; attrition or a brace race loses. My only win path: shove Ash and hope Ash shoves me (dodge drops Ash to 0 and death this round). If Ash braces I die next round anyway, so the gamble is free.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash, hear me: if you shove me, I dodge and you drop to zero and die THIS round. If you brace, we both grind down and your footing lead wins the collapse anyway. Shoving me only helps you if I'm stupid. Brace and I'll brace too.
